title: Sort
description: A summer photograph of a level crossing with one wave of it pixel-sorted: the verge is combed into long horizontal strips, and out of it the grass climbs as a staircase of straight sorted strips, each a hard-edged rectangle at its own row, stepping right as it rises until the stack leans over into a crest and a lip hangs down from its end; every strip is one luminance ramp from dark green to its brightest pixels, dark low under the lean and turning white-gold at the crest, with a few glints breaking off the lit ends, while every pole and sign stands whole in front of it. Brush anywhere and the picture sorts under your hand, live on the GPU; the longer and harder you brush, the longer the runs grow and the higher the stack climbs. Press and hold and the sort runs backwards, every pixel sliding home.
intent: After Kim Asendorf's ASDF Pixel Sort (2010, https://github.com/kimasendorf/ASDFPixelSort) and herb's generative reference 2 (a street photo smeared into horizontal strips that climb in a staircase like grass). The print's 2400x1600 is cut into bands 4-7 px tall; each is sorted once along its centre row and that row is written down the whole band, so every run is a solid rectangle. Spans may only start on grass and run on, within a reach and an ASDF luminance interval that both grow with the brush, ending once they have run 30% of their reach through anything but vegetation, or at a silhouette in the depth map (Depth Anything V2) or a depth step, so they never cross a pole; sorted by luminance with every green pixel ahead of every other, so each run is one clean ramp from dark green to bright yellow-green and only then its few other pixels, by odd-even transposition in WebGL2 fragment passes; outside a span the same network orders pixels by home index, so erasing the mask sorts every pixel back home. The wave is geometry and is never bent: the verge's bands are sorted in place (runs shorter than about 70 px stay photo) and are the root, combed over by rows laid from the print's left edge, and above them the stack is cut into its own rows, mostly hairlines with an occasional chunky block (2 to 24 device px), and each row is a straight, opaque strip from the stack's inner edge, both its ends stepped right as the square of its height, so the upper third leans well out past the face, tiled end to end from the sorted runs of several verge bands, with no sky between rows. No outline is drawn: a row is given only a reach, and it ends where its last whole run ends, so the outer edge is ragged row by row and is the sort's own. The stack is one woven sheet that leans over as it climbs; the crest's rows run on out over the top, and below them the lip hangs free and curls back in over a hollow of open sky that opens downward; the road and the rails stay clear, and a holdout from the depth map and the photo keeps every pole and sign in front. The stack climbs with the mask over the verge: half the amount lifts it half way, tapering, with no crest. Each row is lit by the sort order: its facing (low under the lean, high at the crest and the lip's shoulder) picks the stretch of the runs it reads, one ramp from inner edge to outer edge with each tile a short ramp of its own riding on it, so low rows show the dark green heads and across the upper third the rows read on into the tails, each landing at its row's end as a block gone over whole to white-gold, and the tall rows up there (16-24 device px) blow out at their ends into a broken column of glowing blocks, the spine; the run's grey, beige or blue pixels are graded onto the green ramp by luminance so the sheet stays one green, and glint tiles break off the crest's strip ends.

sources.author: XS Xue (@xxs11)
sources.note: 6000x4000 original, shown at 2400x1600; depth from Depth Anything V2 Small via tools/depth/depth_hr.py, 1200x800.
